subject: Production retry storms & 5xx/429 spike — remediation and credit proposal
messages:
From: Aisha Rao <ops@stratford.health>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: platform@stratford.health
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production timeouts & 5xx spike affecting inference traffic

Hi Ben —

We're seeing a significant spike in 5xx and 429 responses from Redwood starting ~08:50 PDT this morning. Our service reported a ~20% error rate for model: redwood-llama-13b-q4 for about 90 minutes; clients automatically retried requests which amplified load and caused timeouts across our flows.

Impact: several customer-facing flows timed out and we saw elevated latency (p50 -> 850ms, p95 -> 3.2s) and a measurable drop in throughput. We captured traces and a sample of request IDs (attached).

Can you confirm whether this is a service-side issue or a transient client-side behavior? We need an immediate mitigation plan and an ETA for full recovery. We will need documentation for our compliance team and a credit calculation for the impact window.

Attaching: request_ids_20261002.csv, traces_sample.json.

Thanks,
Aisha Rao
Sr. Platform Engineer
Stratford Health

Team — forwarding Stratford's report. They hit a 5xx/429 spike and then retry amplification; they attached traces. Please triage immediately and propose an emergency mitigation we can run without requiring a full rollback. I'm looping in Marissa for customer comms and Sean for SRE coordination.

Immediate asks:
- Is this caused by routing/variant selection or a model runtime regression?
- Can we quickly apply per-account soft rate limits and an account-specific circuit-breaker?
- Estimate scope/time for a permanent fix and a credit amount to offer (ballpark is fine for now).

I'll prepare initial external reply in 30m unless you advise otherwise.

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 15:20:02 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Production timeouts & 5xx spike affecting inference traffic

Ben / team — engineering findings so far (summary):

- Root cause: observed retry amplification from Stratford clients that did not implement exponential backoff; concurrent with a temporary routing imbalance that pushed a disproportionate fraction of Stratford traffic to a slower quantized variant (redwood-llama-13b-q4-slow) under high load.
- Effect: the variant's latency rose non-linearly, backend timeouts increased and upstream health checks began returning 5xx; retries retriggered more load -> classic retry storm.
- Mitigation we applied (completed 03 Oct 10:45 PDT):
  1) Emergency account-level soft throttle at the ingress layer (limit set to 50 rps for Stratford) — reduced immediate error rate to <1%.
  2) Forced traffic reroute to the healthy quantized variant (q4-fast) and disabled the problematic node pool.
  3) Increased short-term autoscaling headroom for the pool serving Stratford.
- Next steps (ETA):
  * Short-term: keep soft throttle and monitor for 24–36 hours.
  * Medium-term (48–72h): adjust routing weights and patch the weight selection heuristic to avoid imbalanced assignments under bursty patterns.
  * Long-term: we will add per-customer adaptive backpressure and a retry-inspecting firewall to break amplification loops.

Credit estimate: finance and I worked a quick calc — based on the 90-minute error window and Stratford's monthly usage, a proportional credit in the range of 12–18% of that invoice period seems reasonable. I attached the quick calc (redwood_credit_calc.xlsx). We can refine after confirming exact impacted token counts.

I'll shadow the account while throttles remain in place; Marissa, please draft the external remediation note and credit proposal.

Hannah
Head of Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rao <ops@stratford.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood remediation steps & proposed credit for Oct 2 incident

Aisha — thanks again for flagging this. Quick update and our proposed next steps: 

What we did
- Temporarily capped Stratford's ingress to 50 rps to stop retry amplification (applied 02 Oct 09:05 PDT).
- Rerouted traffic off the unhealthy variant and removed the problematic node pool.
- Increased autoscaler headroom for your pool; monitoring for 48 hours.

Planned fixes
- Patch to routing heuristic to avoid skewed variant assignment (48–72h).
- Per-customer adaptive backpressure and retry-inspection rules (plan/ETA: 3–4 weeks).

Goodwill & remediation credit
- Proposed immediate goodwill credit: 15% of the invoice for the impacted billing period covering the incident window (our quick estimate — see attached worksheet).
- Additionally, we can provide a one-month trial of a Dedicated capacity slice for Stratford at no charge so you can validate steady throughput under load.

Request: please confirm acceptance of this remediation package by EOD Oct 8 so we can finalize the credit and open a Dedicated trial instance. If you prefer a different credit amount, let us know the supporting impact metrics and we'll escalate.

Attachments: redwood_credit_calc.xlsx, remediation_playbook.md

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Ben — appreciate the quick mitigation and detailed plan. We validated that the throttles and reroute reduced errors; thanks for being responsive.

On the credit: Stratford's compliance and finance teams measured customer-facing impact (delayed care notifications, retries that produced duplicate downstream work). Given downstream remediation costs, we are requesting a 25% credit for the impacted billing period. We can share our incident impact report (high level) if needed.

If Redwood can confirm the 25% credit and provide the Dedicated trial by Oct 12 we will consider the matter resolved. Otherwise we'll need to escalate contract remedies with our procurement org.
